note: Independent source rejudgment against full Section 5, including Section 4.2's locally configured role condition rather than treating a roleless session as an operator bypass of active RFC procedures. TestRFC9234OTCProceduresSurviveOperatorSettings uses strict role configuration and permissive all-role export sets, yet requires exact ingress Provider OTC stamping, Customer OTC withdrawal, upstream egress OTC suppression and downstream local-AS stamping. TestOTCEgressWireBytesCheck independently isolates all three wire-OTC prohibited destinations with no source role configuration or metadata and includes acceptance controls. peerRoleConfig exposes role/strict/export but no procedure override; checkOTCIngress has no operator-policy argument; OTCEgressFilter applies wire-OTC and source-role gates before export policy. otcInsertions marks the active ingress and any-peer egress members Required, and insertForPeer rejects explicit duplicates instead of allowing an operator-positioned member to skip the prepended mandatory filter. Thus the single-polarity rationale is justified for the configured-role procedures; omitting the role is the RFC applicability boundary, not a procedure-modification control. The added destination local role fixtures retain the same assertions. The existing checkOTCIngress producer-break tuple needs renewal because its test unit changed.
